The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=6$ and $y=-3$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-3)^{2} & =4p(6) \\ 9 & =24p \\ p & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=\frac{3}{2}x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{3}{2}x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3}{4y}\end{aligned}
